content.rendered:
I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and to overcome all the power of the enemy. Given. Past tense. Already done. The believer is not searching for authority. The authority has already been placed in their hands.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, July 13, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and to overcome all the power of the enemy; nothing will harm you.”
Luke 10:19 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Luke 10 records one of the most extraordinary scenes in Jesus’ earthly ministry. He sent out seventy-two disciples, two by two, ahead of Him to every town He was about to visit. They went out ordinary. Fishermen. Tax collectors. Everyday men and women with no ministry credentials, no theological degrees, no history of casting out demons. They came back astonished. “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”

Jesus’ response to their report is the founding declaration of the believer’s authority. He did not tell them they were unusually gifted. He did not tell them they had earned a promotion in the Spirit. He told them what was true of every one of them. I have given you authority. Not I will give. Not I might give. I have given. Past tense. Completed action. The authority they had just experienced in the field had been in their hands from the moment He sent them.

The Greek word Jesus uses for “authority” is exousia. It does not mean raw power. It means delegated right. Authorisation. The legal standing to act on behalf of another. A first-century magistrate had exousia over his court. A Roman centurion had exousia over his soldiers. The seventy-two, and every believer after them, have been given exousia by the King of kings Himself. When a believer stands against the enemy in the name of Jesus, they are not standing on their own resources. They are standing on the authority of the One who has sent them.

The imagery Jesus uses is striking. Trampling on snakes and scorpions. It echoes Psalm 91:13, where the psalmist promises the one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will tread on the lion and the serpent. Jesus takes that ancient promise of the Old Testament and hands it to His followers. The enemy under your feet. The powers of darkness disarmed under your heel. And He adds the astonishing closing line. Nothing will harm you. The believer walking in the authority of Christ walks through a spiritually hostile world under a canopy of divine protection.

For Gospelbuzz readers, this is the opening truth of a new two-week series on the believer’s authority in Christ. Over the next fourteen days, we will walk through what the New Testament actually teaches about the authority given to every follower of Jesus, the source it flows from, the tools we exercise it with, and the enemy it defeats. Welcome to “The Believer’s Authority.” Today, the foundation. The authority has already been given. You are not asking. You are walking in what is already yours.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I have been given authority in Christ Jesus. The authority to trample on snakes and scorpions. The authority to overcome all the power of the enemy. This authority has not been earned. It has been delegated to me by the King of kings Himself. I stand today in the exousia of Christ, and every dark thing that would rise against my life, my family, my calling is under my feet in His name. Nothing will harm me because I walk in what You have already given. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have been given authority in Christ. The power of the enemy is under my feet in His name. Nothing will harm me. I walk in the exousia of the King today.
